system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team | **Prepared by:** AI legal assistant (buyer side) | **Date:** 6 Nov 2026
**Status of source material:** Seller's draft and Disclosure Letter are the counterparty's documents. Nothing in them is "agreed", "final" or "market" because the Seller says so (playbook 0.4/6.3). Note the Disclosure Letter is cut off at **5.00pm 22 September 2026** – it is six weeks stale and must be refreshed before signing.

---

## A. Overall assessment

The Seller's cover note describes the package as "fair and balanced". It is not. On almost every limitation point the Seller has taken a position *beyond* our rejected end of the range, and in several places the Seller Update contradicts the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (e.g. the Update says Bluefen is "addressed"; the Disclosure Letter admits no consent has been delivered). The Disclosure Letter is actually more candid than the Update and should be used against the Update.

Headline departures:
1. Liability regime (cap, thresholds, time, scope) is wholesale off-playbook.
2. Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP and specific indemnities are being collapsed into the general regime.
3. No fraud carve-out anywhere; limitations expressly apply to "all Claims of any nature".
4. Blanket deemed disclosure and blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion.
5. Both key Completion risks (Bluefen consent; Riverlark payout) are unresolved and the Seller proposes to defer them past Completion.
6. AUD 420,000 of bonuses silently excluded from the funds flow.

---

## B. Clause-by-clause analysis

### 1. Clause 12.1 – General Warranty cap
**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Playbook:** Open at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. 20% is a *conditional fallback* requiring prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. **None has been given.**
**Reasoning:** The fact that the Seller's number coincides with our fallback is irrelevant; a position is not cleared merely because a number matches (playbook 6.3). We also have no reason to concede the cap when the Seller has given nothing on thresholds, time or scope.
**Push back:** Hold at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is available.

### 2. Clause 12.2 – Thresholds
**Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery.
**Playbook:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** (tipping) basket.
**Reasoning:** Seller's de minimis is 5x ours and the basket 5x ours, and the basket is a true deductible rather than a tipping basket. Combined with the 20% cap this materially erodes real recovery. There is no justification offered.
**Push back:** Revert to 5,000 / 50,000 / first dollar. Confirm Fundamental/Title, Tax (when settled), specific indemnities and fraud sit outside both thresholds.

### 3. Clause 12.3 / 13 – Time limits and the "all Claims" default
**Seller:** 18 months for General Warranty Claims; *plus* "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
**Playbook:** 24 months general; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given). Separate regimes for Fundamental/Title (6+ years), Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims; **no hidden general-regime override.**
**Reasoning:** Two problems. (a) 18 months is unauthorised. (b) The "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default is precisely the hidden override the playbook prohibits – it flips the drafting burden onto us and would, by default, drag Title, Tax, IP, indemnity and covenant claims into the 18-month / 20% / basket regime unless we catch every instance.
**Push back:** 24 months. Delete the default-application sentence and replace with the reverse: limitations in clause 12 apply *only* to General Warranty Claims unless a clause expressly extends them.

### 4. Fundamental / Title Warranties
**Seller:** Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
**Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
**Reasoning:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Title and capacity are the foundation of the deal; a 20% cap on title means we could pay AUD 24m and recover AUD 4.8m if we acquired nothing. This is a non-negotiable for the buyer.
**Push back:** Reject outright. Insert full Fundamental Warranty regime.

### 5. Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature"
**Seller:** Universal application; no carve-out.
**Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one on our side may waive this.
**Reasoning:** The draft contains **no fraud carve-out at all**. As drafted it purports to cap and time-bar fraud claims and to exclude reliance on fraudulent statements. Quite apart from being off-playbook, this is likely unenforceable in part under NSW law, but we should not rely on a court to fix the drafting.
**Push back:** Insert an overriding carve-out clause: nothing in the SPA limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller or its related persons. Also carve specific indemnities and Fundamental Warranties out of the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language.

### 6. Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2 – General disclosure
**Seller:** Whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 22 Sep 2026, plus Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" deemed disclosed.
**Playbook:** Specific **fair** disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
**Reasoning:** General data-room disclosure neutralises the warranties: anything buried in any document is "disclosed" regardless of whether a reasonable buyer could identify the breach. Public-register disclosure is open-ended and unverifiable. Paragraph 1.4 (no admission of anything) is standard but, read with 1.1, means the Seller discloses everything and admits nothing.
**Push back:** Disclosure limited to matters *fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter* in the specific disclosures of the Disclosure Letter (and the documents expressly referenced against each). Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Require an updated letter brought down to signing and (if there is a gap) to Completion, with no new disclosures permitted to cure warranty breaches.

### 7. Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge
**Seller:** No claim for any matter of which Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
**Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must be limited to named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
**Reasoning:** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that, combined with general disclosure, would make the warranties almost worthless. Imputing advisers' knowledge is also unacceptable. This clause and the disclosure regime are a belt-and-braces attempt to achieve the same exclusion twice.
**Push back:** Delete 8.3 entirely. If any knowledge concept survives, it attaches only to the Seller's warranties (Seller's Knowledge = actual knowledge of named individuals after due enquiry), not to the Buyer's right to claim.

### 8. Clause 3 / 6.3 – Bluefen consent
**Seller Update:** "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent.
**Seller Disclosure Letter para 2:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% FY26 revenue; change-control clause 11.2 with conditions at 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence conditions satisfied.**
**Playbook:** Effective consent **and** evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied, before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient for a material customer.
**Reasoning:** The Update and the Disclosure Letter are inconsistent – the Update says "addressed", the Letter admits nothing has been obtained. A conditional consent delivered but with 11.3 conditions unmet is not an effective consent; "deemed satisfied on delivery" would let a conditional or defective letter satisfy the CP. For 30% of revenue this is a genuine Completion condition, not an endeavours covenant.
**Push back:** Hard CP: unconditional written consent from Bluefen under clause 11.2 in agreed form, together with evidence satisfactory to Buyer (acting reasonably) that each 11.3 condition is satisfied or waived by Bluefen. Seller to use all reasonable endeavours (not merely reasonable) to procure; Buyer right not to complete, and long-stop date. Request current status since 22 Sep – the position may have moved.

### 9. Clause 2 / 7 – Riverlark facility
**Seller Update:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion".
**Disclosure Letter para 3:** Not repaid; no final discharge of security; change-of-control 8.1 and discharge mechanics 9.2.
**Playbook:** Current payout letter; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
**Reasoning:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. Completing with AUD 3.2m of secured bank debt outstanding, a change-of-control default under 8.1 triggered by our acquisition, and only a promise of a later release, exposes us to enforcement risk against the Company's assets we have just paid full price for. The ~AUD 3.2m figure is also dated and must be refreshed.
**Push back:** Completion deliverables: (i) payout letter from Riverlark dated within 5 business days of Completion; (ii) Buyer pays the payout amount direct to Riverlark out of the Purchase Price per the funds flow; (iii) executed deeds of release and PPSR discharge (or Riverlark's irrevocable undertaking to lodge discharges on receipt of funds), with the CoC waiver under 8.1 if repayment occurs post-Completion by any margin. If the Seller insists on post-Completion release, it goes to Amelia Frost for decision, not to the deal team.

### 10. Funds flow – DD-005 Completion bonuses
**Seller Update:** AUD 420,000 bonuses "a matter for the Seller", not itemised.
**Disclosure Letter para 5:** Conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000; **not in draft funds flow**; silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
**Playbook:** Must be a specific line item or seller-funded, plus triggered on-costs; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Reasoning:** These bonuses are triggered by *our* Completion and will be paid by the Company (which we own post-Completion). If they are not deducted from price or funded by the Seller, we pay them twice – once in price and once in cash. "A matter for the Seller" is the correct principle but the funds flow does not implement it. On-costs (super, payroll tax, possibly leave loading) could add a meaningful percentage; we should not assume a figure but must require the Seller to quantify.
**Push back:** Either (a) treat the gross bonuses plus all on-costs as Transaction Bonuses deducted from the Purchase Price and paid through payroll at Completion, or (b) Seller indemnity for the full gross-up amount, with a specific line item in the funds flow in either case. Request the bonus letters and a quantified on-cost schedule.

### 11. Clause 11.1 – Ironquay IP indemnity
**Seller Update:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
**Disclosure Letter para 4:** DD-004 cl 7.3 – SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is not bank verification; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
**Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 is not verified either way.
**Reasoning:** The real risk is not the AUD 180,000 payment – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 deliverables (and anything built on them) until payment clears. An indemnity limited to the fee does not cover loss of IP, third-party claims, re-work or any customer-facing consequences. "Considered adequate" is the Seller's opinion. Equally, we must not state that the fee is unpaid as a fact – DD-010 is an internal ledger.
**Push back:** (i) Pre-Completion: Seller to procure cleared payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, delivered at Completion (preserves the 7.3 cure). (ii) Indemnity broadened to cover any failure of title to SOW3 Project Materials, third-party infringement claims arising from Ironquay deliverables, and costs of perfecting title – outside the general cap/basket/time regime. (iii) Request bank evidence of payment status either way.

### 12. Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 – DD-006 export/privacy incident
**Seller Update:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
**Disclosure Letter para 6:** Download link sent to unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether accessed, exact scope, or whether notification required; investigation preliminary; no loss stated.
**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
**Reasoning:** "Not expected to be material" is an untested assertion on an admittedly incomplete investigation. We should neither accept that characterisation nor inflate the matter. The correct posture is procedural: lock down the evidence and allocate the risk.
**Push back:** Covenant to preserve all access/download logs and link-expiry records; complete the investigation (including whether the link was accessed/revoked) and report before signing; specific disclosure updated; specific indemnity for costs of any notification, regulatory response and third-party claims arising from the DD-006 incident, sitting outside the general regime. No price adjustment proposed at this stage.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000)
**Seller Update:** "Ordinary-course operating costs."
**Disclosure Letter para 8:** Three related renewals at AUD 110,000 each; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Reasoning:** The Seller's label is a conclusion the Letter itself does not support. Three "related" renewals of identical size read together suggest a single arrangement possibly split; timing relative to Completion and the locked-box/completion-accounts mechanics matters.
**Push back:** Request the contracts, renewal/termination dates and whether any amount is accrued or prepaid at Completion. Reserve position on treatment (Debt-like item, working capital, or genuinely ordinary course) pending that information. Add a specific warranty that no supplier renewals above an agreed threshold have been entered into outside the ordinary course since the Accounts Date.

### 14. Tax / IP warranties
**Seller Update:** "Settled under the general regime above."
**Playbook:** Tax and IP terms **remain OPEN**; separate categories; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution assumed.
**Reasoning:** Nothing has been settled. The Seller is attempting to close these points by assertion and, via the clause 13 default-application language, to subject them to the 18-month / 20% / basket regime. Tax in particular would ordinarily carry a separate cap and a longer period aligned with assessment periods; IP (particularly given Ironquay) warrants its own treatment.
**Push back:** Record Tax and IP as open items; propose a Tax Indemnity and separate Tax Warranty regime (period and cap to be agreed) and a separate IP warranty/indemnity regime. Do not accept any drafting that defaults them into clause 12.

### 15. Title evidence – DD-012
**Seller Update:** Title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012."
**Disclosure Letter para 10:** DD-012 is the source relied on; does **not** say the Buyer has verified.
**Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof.
**Reasoning:** A company's own register is prepared by the Seller's appointees and can be wrong or out of date. It says nothing about encumbrances (PPSR, Riverlark security over shares?), options, pre-emptive rights in the constitution or shareholder agreements, or the Seller's own authority to sell.
**Push back:** Buyer to obtain current ASIC company extract, PPSR searches against the Company and the Seller, the constitution and any shareholder agreements, share certificates (or indemnity for lost certificates), board minutes approving the transfer and Seller's constitutional/board authority. Completion deliverables to include executed transfers, certificates and updated register. Fundamental Warranties on title and capacity as per item 4.

### 16. Lesser items – Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
Disclosure Letter frames these as notification only (lease) and an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale (Mossvale). These framings are plausible but are the Seller's reading. **Action:** our DD team to confirm the lease clause is notification-only and whether it has been given; confirm the Mossvale clause has no change-of-control limb. Low priority unless DD shows otherwise.

---

## C. Process and credibility points

- **Internal inconsistency:** Seller Update says Bluefen is "addressed" and funds flow is "agreed"; Disclosure Letter says no Bluefen consent, Riverlark unpaid, bonuses excluded. Quote the Letter back to the Seller.
- **"Agreed price mechanics":** we have not agreed a funds flow that excludes AUD 420k of Completion bonuses and defers AUD 3.2m of secured debt. Nothing in the funds flow should be treated as agreed.
- **Staleness:** Disclosure Letter is as at 22 Sep 2026. Require a refreshed data room cut-off and bring-down disclosure; ask specifically for post-22 Sep developments on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay payment and DD-006.
- **Authority discipline:** Two Seller numbers (20% cap, 18 months) coincide with our fallbacks. Neither is authorised. The team should not reference or hint at those fallbacks in correspondence. Any move requires Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the draft.
- **Fraud carve-out:** no one on the deal team has authority to trade this.

---

## D. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | Hold 25% / 6.0m; no fallback signalled |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k / excess only | 5k / 50k / first dollar |
| 3 | Time limit | 18 months + "applies to all Claims" default | 24 months; delete default; limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | 100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge |
| 5 | Fraud | No carve-out; limitations apply to all claims | Full carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct – non-waivable |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public registers | Specific fair disclosure only; delete 1.1/1.2; bring-down letter |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. advisers and "discoverable" | Delete 8.3 |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; deemed satisfied on delivery | Hard CP: effective consent + evidence 11.3 conditions met |
| 9 | Riverlark | Release after Completion | Payout letter, direct repayment from funds, releases at Completion; post-Completion only with irrevocable undertaking + A. Frost approval |
| 10 | Bonuses | Not in funds flow | Line item or Seller-funded, gross of on-costs; quantify on-costs |
| 11 | Ironquay | SOW3 fee only | Pay fees + confirmatory assignment at Completion; broadened IP indemnity outside general regime |
| 12 | DD-006 | "Not material" | Preserve logs, complete investigation, updates, specific indemnity; no assumption of breach or quantum |
| 13 | Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | Obtain contracts; assess; reserve treatment; no automatic deduction |
| 14 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | OPEN; separate regimes; no default into cl 12 |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent ASIC/PPSR/constitutional/authority evidence; Fundamental Warranties |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only / no consent | DD to confirm; low priority |

**Recommended next step:** Issue a mark-up and issues list on the above, lead with the structural points (items 3–5, 8, 9) since they determine whether the rest of the package has any value, and request refreshed disclosure before responding on price-sensitive items (10, 13). Escalate to Amelia Frost only if the Seller refuses to move on cap/time and the team wishes to consider the fallbacks – not before.
=== END ADVICE ===
